answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by bonding every identity: each newcomer posts collateral from a scarce, rate-limited resource before its votes count, so ten thousand clones mean ten thousand stakes. A comet of coordinated sockpuppets leaves an overlapping endorsement graph, and the slashing rule drains every bond in that cluster, so the attacker burns more than the swarm can farm. Honest agents lose only normal operating risk. A garden shows it: one seed is cheap, but a whole plot needs land. Evading this means splitting across registries, which a thin karst of liquidity cannot fund.
